feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong CV with clear senior-level positioning, credible progression, and relevant digital strategy depth. It reads polished and substantive, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with limited quantified outcomes beyond scope metrics; a few style/grammar inconsistencies also reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing responsibility and leadership credibility.  
- Strong domain alignment for digital communications/strategy roles, with solid coverage of web, analytics, content, and multimedia.  
- Good use of concrete platform/tool references and scale indicators like “10,000+ page website” and “3.5 million annual page views.”

1. Top improvements  
- Add more impact/results metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include improvements in traffic, engagement, efficiency, campaign performance, cost savings, or team/process gains.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” Consolidating these sections would improve structure and save space.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; use consistent serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); “front-end” and date abbreviations/punctuation should be standardized throughout.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it’s slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding one clearer differentiator would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Lead with your strongest current value: enterprise digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with “multi-channel digital communications” to reduce listiness.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving multi-channel communications, web modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, CMS and workflow design, and stakeholder coordination across complex teams. Strong background in advocacy and policy communications, translating technical issues into clear, accessible content and scalable digital systems.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflow/systems,” and “stakeholder coordination” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” also appears throughout the experience section; keep it brief here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening wording and emphasizing higher-value, more distinctive capabilities will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, senior-level terms: “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership”; “Web & CMS administration” → “Web platform governance & CMS modernization.”
- Reduce overlap and group related items for clarity; suggested version: Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform governance & CMS modernization • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow automation & systems architecture • Public-sector policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, video & live event production
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout and standardize style/capitalization.
- Consider dropping “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” here since it reads more like a soft skill than a core competency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, editorial systems, analytics, and multimedia.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills almost exactly.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten the bullets, foreground strategic outcomes, and avoid repeating NACo achievements already covered in prior roles and Recent Projects.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, content operations, and enterprise communications systems as an external consultant.”
- Convert task-heavy bullets into 3–4 outcome-oriented bullets; e.g. “Built cross-team workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia channels.”
- Combine overlapping technical bullets: merge CMS/front-end/troubleshooting with Drupal microsite work into one concise implementation bullet.
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, workflow time saved, search/discovery improvements, stakeholder groups served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search initiative” overlaps with Recent Projects; keep one brief mention here and let the project section carry the detail.
- Governance, analytics, and Drupal modernization also echo the Director role; emphasize external advisory/consulting scope and new initiatives only.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise ownership and outcomes while avoiding overlap with the adjacent NACo roles on newsletters, video, and day-to-day channel management.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine and prioritize the biggest wins: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add % improvements in publishing speed, reporting efficiency, engagement, production cost savings, or reduced agency/vendor reliance from the in-house studio.
- Rephrase softer bullets to show business impact: “Implemented governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency, accountability, and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, not routine channel execution.
- Video studio bullet may overlap with older video-production entries; stress that this was a first-of-its-kind organizational capability build.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads broad and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Tighten it around what was distinctly built or expanded at this level, with sharper verbs and any available scale/results.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize ownership and scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging for a national public-sector audience.”
- Combine and tighten bullets around measurable outputs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-focused: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Clarify operational impact: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry; avoid repeating channel oversight language.
- Video-program language also overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager role and Recent Projects; keep this version focused on expansion/operationalization.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter and emphasize higher-value leadership themes not already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:  
  **• Enterprise digital strategy & transformation • Editorial governance & content operations • Cross-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Audience-centered content strategy**
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” or “strategy” to sound more senior and operationally aligned.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixed constructions like “audience-focused content planning” beside broader leadership terms.
- If space allows, make one item more distinctive to recent work, e.g. **AI-informed content discovery strategy** or **enterprise web governance**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications leadership” overlap heavily with the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is also echoed in Core Competencies; tighten or replace to avoid repetition.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill coverage, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes rather than repeat a software list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Remove lower-priority or older-signal items like jQuery unless it is still central to current work.
- Group related items for concision: combine “Drupal / WordPress / SharePoint / Power Pages” into “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms” if those platforms are not all recent or equally important.
- If possible, align with proven outcomes from recent roles, such as “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “AI-enabled legislative search,” elsewhere in the CV rather than here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Nearly all items duplicate the Technical + IT section; keep this section more strategic.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also repeats Core Competencies and recent project language.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-level capability and decision-making rather than repeat software names.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tool list to strategic outcomes: “Analytics strategy, KPI frameworks, executive dashboards, user behavior analysis, SEO/performance optimization.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools if needed: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI/Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Tighten phrasing and group related items: replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” and “SEO and performance analysis” with “SEO and conversion/performance insights.”
- Suggested rewrite: “- Analytics strategy and KPI design - Executive reporting and dashboard development - User behavior and journey analysis - SEO and performance optimization - GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current item duplicates the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” entry in Technical + IT almost exactly.
- Since recent NACo experience already proves these tools, Topline Skills should stay more strategic and less tool-heavy.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and several NACo bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing production scope and technical/event-delivery capability rather than generic “video production.”

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as tighter, more specialized skills: “Broadcast video production • Livestream and webcast delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Hybrid/virtual event production • Post-production editing”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast video production” or “Studio and field video production” to sound more senior and less generic.
- If space allows, add one qualifier tied to recent work: “Built and operated in-house studio workflows” or “Supported advocacy programming and live event coverage.”
- Keep terms parallel and noun-based; avoid mixing broad functions with tools unless the tool is a differentiator.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “multimedia production” already appear in Core Competencies; use more specific phrasing here to avoid repetition.
- “Studio operations” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media bullet about building an in-house studio.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, scannable list, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Since Drupal is central to recent roles, this item should either sharpen platform emphasis or be merged to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider adding context: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, make Drupal more specific to match recent impact: **Drupal 9/10** or **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; enterprise governance)**
- Keep this item platform-only; move anything about modernization, integrations, or technical execution to the adjacent coding/technical section
- Consider renaming the title to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills entry almost exactly
- “GitHub Pages” may be too minor unless it supported a notable project; cut it if space is tight

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current and implementation-focused by emphasizing tools you actively use in recent Drupal/search/automation work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Tighten and modernize the list: **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions**
- Drop **jQuery** unless it is still actively used in current projects; if kept, place last to avoid dating the profile.
- If space allows, add one specificity cue tied to recent work, e.g. **front-end implementation for Drupal, serverless scripting, deployment automation**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills → keep the stronger version in one place.
- **Google Tag Manager** may fit better under **Data, Analytics & Optimization** unless you want this section strictly implementation-oriented.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere, so tighten and frame around higher-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Reorder by relevance to recent work and systems leadership: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams
- Remove lower-signal or older tools unless still actively used: Basecamp, Trello
- If space allows, add light functional grouping for clarity: Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Jira/Asana/Slack/Teams are useful, but too many collaboration tools can dilute stronger automation credentials.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. It should signal level of use and avoid repeating email leadership already covered in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Rename for specificity: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Add level/context if accurate: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (enterprise journeys, segmentation, campaign ops) • Higher Logic (member communications) • Mailchimp**
- Order by strongest/recentest platform first; if Dynamics 365 is most current, keep it first.
- If one tool was only light exposure, either drop it or qualify it elsewhere; a shorter, stronger list reads better than broad but shallow coverage.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Your work experience already shows leadership of email/newsletter operations; don’t restate outcomes here unless tied to platform-specific capability.
- “Engagement” may overlap with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies; keep this item tool-focused.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, site refresh support, and multimedia production.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and support day-to-day operations across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Split into 2–3 bullets with clearer actions: supported website refresh; produced livestreams/weekly video updates; improved workflows and supervised/mentored one associate.
- Replace soft phrases like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows” with concrete outcomes, tools, or volume if available (e.g., number of livestreams, cadence of video series, size/timing of website refresh).
- Tighten wording: remove “contributed to” where you had ownership; use stronger verbs like “helped launch,” “produced,” “streamlined,” “guided.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or establishing the format, not expanding it.
- “First in-house digital team” may echo later leadership claims; keep this role focused on foundational buildout rather than enterprise leadership.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize coordination + launch impact, and trim broad support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the clearest outcome: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; translated findings into digital and multimedia content.”
- Tighten the podcast line: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If you can, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Consider a two-part structure: research/program support first, then digital/media contribution second, to show progression toward later communications roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is too close to later digital/media entries; keep this item lighter and more foundational.
- Avoid overemphasizing video/multimedia here since those strengths are better demonstrated in 2015–2024 roles.
